title: Cayenne compress for joint pain
subtitle: A warming external compress of Capsicum annuum for arthritic and muscular joint pain
excerpt: Cayenne compress is a cloth soaked in hot capsicum-infused water and applied directly to the skin over a painful joint. The capsaicin in cayenne temporarily depletes substance P, the neuropeptide that carries pain signals, in the surface nerves. Used externally for arthritic joint pain, neuralgia, and post-injury inflammation. A single compress session lasts 15 to 20 minutes. Never apply to broken skin.
sourceNotes: Felter & Lloyd, King's American Dispensatory (1898), capsicum entry. Maud Grieve, A Modern Herbal (1931), cayenne entry, Botanical.com. Capsaicin mechanism documented in: Holzer P., Capsaicin: Cellular targets, mechanisms of action, and selectivity for thin sensory neurons, Pharmacological Reviews (1991).

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Prepare fresh for each session. Do not store the cayenne-infused water.

glossaryTerms.definition: A neuropeptide that carries pain signals from peripheral nerves to the spinal cord and brain. Capsaicin causes nerve endings to release substance P all at once and then prevents its re-synthesis for a period, creating initial warmth or slight burning followed by reduced local pain sensitivity.

A substance that causes redness and warmth in the skin when applied externally, by drawing blood to the surface and creating a local counter-irritant effect. Cayenne is one of the most potent herbal rubefacients.

content.text: Cayenne compress is a cloth wrung out in hot capsicum-infused water and held against a painful joint for 15 to 20 minutes. A traditional
preparation for arthritic joint pain, neuralgia, and stiff muscles. Capsaicin, the active compound of cayenne, works by depleting

from local nerve endings, causing initial warmth and sometimes mild tingling, followed by a period of reduced pain sensitivity. The effect is localised and temporary. Wear gloves when handling the prepared cloth.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body: Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor before use. Full precautions are in the 'When not to use' section.

content.text: Put on kitchen gloves. Stir 1 teaspoon of cayenne powder into 300 ml of hot water (70 to 75 °C) in a small bowl. Stir well.
Soak a folded muslin cloth or thick flannel in the cayenne water. Wring out so it is damp but not dripping.
Test the temperature against the inner wrist before applying to a joint, it should be comfortably hot, not burning. Apply to the affected joint and cover with a dry cloth to retain heat.
Leave in place for 15 to 20 minutes. Expect a sensation of warmth and mild tingling from the capsaicin. Remove if the sensation becomes uncomfortable.
After removing, wash the skin with mild soap and water. Wash hands and gloves thoroughly.

Once or twice daily for acute joint pain. For chronic arthritis, daily use for 2 to 4 weeks provides cumulative benefit as substance P is progressively depleted. Reduce frequency once pain levels improve.
Cayenne powder stores 12 months in a sealed jar away from light. Prepare the compress liquid fresh for each session.
When not to use this remedy

Do not apply to broken, infected, or inflamed skin. Do not use if the joint is hot and acutely inflamed (gout flare, acute rheumatoid flare, or suspected joint infection), heat-based preparations worsen acute inflammation. See a doctor for joint swelling that is rapid, severe, or accompanied by fever.
